steps: A supercritical state is formed when a substance is above its critical temperature and critical pressure.
In this state, the liquid and gas phases become indistinguishable.
It behaves as a fluid with properties intermediate between those of a liquid and a gas.
items.finalAnswer: A supercritical state is a fluid state in which the liquid and gas phases are indistinguishable.

steps: A fluorescent tube contains a gas at low pressure.
When a high voltage is applied across the tube, an electric discharge passes through the gas.
The discharge ionizes the gas, producing free electrons and positive ions.
This ionized gas is plasma; it produces ultraviolet radiation that makes the fluorescent coating glow.
items.finalAnswer: An electric discharge ionizes the low-pressure gas in the tube, creating plasma.

steps: Organic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with carbon compounds, generally excluding carbonates, bicarbonates and oxides of carbon.
Biochemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with the chemical substances and processes occurring in living organisms.
items.finalAnswer: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, whereas biochemistry studies the substances and chemical processes of living organisms.

steps: Diamond has a high refractive index, so light entering it is strongly refracted and undergoes repeated total internal reflection.
This repeated reflection gives diamond its brilliance.
Cutting and polishing diamond into many faces can increase its brilliance by causing more internal reflection.
items.finalAnswer: Diamond’s high refractive index causes repeated total internal reflection; cutting and polishing it into many faces can enhance its brilliance.

steps: Water molecules are polar: the oxygen end is partially negative and the hydrogen ends are partially positive.
The partially negative oxygen ends attract Na⁺ ions, while the partially positive hydrogen ends attract Cl⁻ ions.
Water molecules surround and separate the ions from the ionic crystal; this process is called hydration.
The hydrated ions disperse throughout the water: NaCl(s) → Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq).
items.finalAnswer: Polar water molecules hydrate and separate Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, dissolving sodium chloride.

steps: The solubility of a compound depends on the nature of the solute and the solvent.
It depends on how strongly the solute particles attract one another compared with how strongly they are attracted to the solvent particles.
Different compounds therefore have different solubilities in water at the same temperature.
items.finalAnswer: Different solute–solute and solute–water attractions give compounds different solubilities in water.

steps: The solubility of sodium chloride changes very little with temperature.
The solubility of potassium nitrate increases greatly as temperature rises.
On cooling a hot saturated solution, much potassium nitrate crystallizes out, whereas little sodium chloride crystallizes.
items.finalAnswer: NaCl solubility changes little with temperature, unlike KNO₃, so cooling a solution crystallizes much less NaCl.

steps: Graphite consists of layers of carbon atoms.
The forces between these layers are weak, so the layers can slide over one another easily.
This softness and easy sliding make graphite slippery to touch and useful as a lubricant.
items.finalAnswer: Graphite is slippery because its weakly bonded layers slide over one another; this property enables its use as a lubricant.
